A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 26-page versions of the same work, including the main text, figures, tables, Appendix A proofs and Appendix B practical considerations. Text comparison and rendered-page checks establish reliable comparability.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original evaluations on VAERS myocarditis reports and simulated reporting from HMDA mortgage data, including stopping times, identified-group relative risks and permutation analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains the original vaccine and mortgage evaluations in Section 5, Tables 1–2 and Figures 2–3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and its sequential Z-test and betting-style implementations retain identical statistics, thresholds, Online Newton Step updates and Bonferroni correction. Renaming the database does not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use VAERS reports with VaxView reference data and 2019 HMDA mortgage data. The populations, subgroup definitions and correlated, all-denials and anti-correlated reporting scenarios remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain the asymptotic Z-test, finite-sample Z-test and betting-style test. Figure 3 also retains the same comparisons with and without Bonferroni correction.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 retain the preprocessing, 29 vaccine groups, 115 mortgage groups, alpha of 0.1, beta grids, minimum stopping times of 25 and 50, and mortgage trial limit of 40,000 steps.

E4.justification: Report-order robustness in Figure 2, the Bonferroni analysis in Figure 3, and sensitivity to beta and mortgage reporting behavior are unchanged. Neither appendix adds or removes an analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 random permutations for the vaccine robustness analysis and each mortgage configuration, using the same cumulative trial-count plots and averages. Run-count, seed and uncertainty-reporting practices do not change.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2, Figures 2–3 and their reported findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 at beta = 2 retains stopping times of 34, 69 and 61 reports for males aged 18–29 under the asymptotic Z-test, finite-sample Z-test and betting-style test, respectively.

T1.justification: The assumptions, definitions, Propositions 3.2 and 3.4, Theorems 4.1–4.4 and Appendix A proofs are unchanged. The terminology substitution in Appendix B changes no mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same contributions: aggregating individual reports through subgroup sequential tests, connecting reporting assumptions to harm, providing validity and power guarantees, and demonstrating rapid identification in two applications.

C2.justification: Interpretations of relative risk and incidence, stopping-time tradeoffs, reporting assumptions and practical limitations remain unchanged. Section 1.1 already distinguished individual-report databases from accident catalogs in v1; v2 retains that distinction.

D1.justification: Data filtering, subgroup construction, simulated reporting probabilities and implementation parameters are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same experimental code link and pointer to data-download and preprocessing instructions.

R1.justification: The cited works and reference list are unchanged. Relationships to fairness auditing, contestability, sequential testing and accident catalogs remain substantively identical; the database renaming introduces no new research-positioning claim.

P1.justification: V2 replaces many uses of 'incident database' with 'reporting database' across the abstract, introduction, model setup, discussion and Appendix B. It also changes one introductory phrase to 'individual reporting systems.' These are limited terminology edits; the narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1's caption changes from 'incident database framework' to 'reporting database framework,' while the diagram remains unchanged. Terminology edits cause modest text reflow, including paragraph continuations across pages 2–4. Result figures and tables retain their displays and placement.

improvement.justification: Using 'reporting database' more consistently aligns the abstract and framework description with Section 1.1's existing distinction from accident catalogs. This modestly reduces terminological ambiguity. The benefit is limited to clarity: methods, results, proofs, limitations and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
